name: google-chat-mcp
description: Google Chat as MCP tools: read, search and write to your spaces, direct messages and sidebar.
long_description:
A single Go binary that speaks MCP over stdio, on your own machine, against your own Google account. macOS, Windows and Linux, on both architectures each. There is no server to host and no service account.

You need your own Google OAuth client and one login before the bundle works. Create an OAuth 2.0 Client ID of type Desktop app, download the JSON, and pick it during install. Then run `google-chat-mcp login --client-secret <that file>` once from a terminal; the refresh token goes to your OS keyring. The README has the full setup.

The bundle asks for the same settings as a client's configuration file, each off or empty unless you set it. The tools that cannot be taken back stay unregistered until you turn them on, and attachment transfer stays off until you pick a folder.

client_secret.title: OAuth client JSON
client_secret.description: The client_secret JSON you downloaded when you created the Desktop OAuth client. The same file you passed to `google-chat-mcp login`.

profile.title: Profile
profile.description: Which stored login to use. Separate profiles keep separate tokens, such as a work account and a personal one, and each is logged in to with `google-chat-mcp login --profile <name>`. A name is up to 64 characters from a to z, 0 to 9, - and _, starting with a letter or digit; capitals are read as lowercase, and any other name stops the server at start. Leave it empty for the default profile.

read_only.title: Read-only
read_only.description: Register only the tools that change nothing in Chat. Read-only wins over Deleting, and what cannot be taken back: with both on, the tools that cannot be taken back stay unregistered. For Google to refuse a write as well, log in with `google-chat-mcp login --read-only=true`, which asks for read-only scopes. Turning writes back on takes another login.

enable_destructive.title: Deleting, and what cannot be taken back
enable_destructive.description: Register the tools that delete messages, threads, spaces, sections and custom emoji, remove a member, open a space to an audience, make someone a manager and add someone from outside your organization. Each call also needs confirm: true. Off by default, and Read-only wins: with Read-only on, this registers nothing. This server asks nobody before a call, so Claude Desktop's approval of each tool is then the only check.

toolsets.title: Toolsets
toolsets.description: Comma-separated tool groups to register, or all. The groups are core, sections, pins, emoji, events, readstate, settings, availability, admin. core is always on. Leave it empty for every group but admin. Only a Workspace administrator can use admin, and its scope needs a login run with `--toolsets all,admin`.

local_dir.title: Attachment folder
local_dir.description: The one folder attachments are downloaded to and uploaded from. Leave it empty and this server touches no files.
